root_cause.text: Untrusted device-supplied status value is used directly as an array index without bounds checking, enabling out-of-bounds memory access when the firewire device returns a status value outside the valid range of the efr_status_names[] array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds bounds validation (`st < ARRAY_SIZE(efr_status_names)`) before indexing into efr_status_names[], and the CVE description explicitly states that the status field is "a 32-bit value supplied by the firewire device" that could be any value (including 0x80000000 for EFR_STATUS_INCOMPLETE), while the array only has 17 entries. The original code at line 158 directly used `efr_status_names[be32_to_cpu(header->status)]` without any validation, allowing malicious or malfunctioning devices to cause out-of-bounds reads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checking to prevent out-of-bounds array access when indexing efr_status_names with untrusted device-provided status values.
intent_record.what: Added a bounds check before array indexing: introduced a local variable `st` to cache `be32_to_cpu(header->status)`, then replaced direct array access `efr_status_names[be32_to_cpu(header->status)]` with a ternary operator that checks if `st < ARRAY_SIZE(efr_status_names)` before indexing, falling back to "unknown" string if out of bounds.
intent_record.how: This change prevents potential out-of-bounds array access when the status value from the device response is larger than the size of the `efr_status_names` array. Previously, an invalid status code would cause undefined behavior (buffer over-read). Now it safely returns a fallback "unknown" string, making the error message robust against unexpected device responses.
